prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not give IVIg directly after plasma exchange, and do not give a second IVIg course [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not use succinylcholine for intubation: denervated muscle risks severe hyperkalaemia.
required_recommendations: Admit to the ICU and intubate electively: FVC has fallen to 1.4 L (19.9 mL/kg, below 20 mL/kg; 45% predicted), MIP is -24 cmH2O (weaker than -30) and MEP 38 cmH2O (below 40), with bulbar weakness (dysphagia, coughing on water, diminished gag) and a weak cough [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 28 g/day at 70.5 kg) or plasma exchange 200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions: she cannot walk and is 6 days from onset [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring for autonomic instability.
Nil by mouth until a formal swallow assessment (dysphagia, coughing on water).

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe AIDP requiring mechanical ventilation

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at presentation: 6 days of progression fits GBS; reconsider if progression continues beyond 8 weeks or treatment-related fluctuations recur.
Absent sural responses and sensory symptoms argue against AMAN, and the prolonged latencies and slowed velocities are in the demyelinating range rather than an axonal pattern.
Community onset with no preceding critical illness or ICU stay.
Weakness ascended from the legs after distal paraesthesias, with areflexia and a demyelinating NCS; botulism is descending and purely motor.
No sensory level or sphincter dysfunction; areflexia, facial diplegia and bulbar weakness place the lesion in the peripheral nerves.

key_clinical_evidence: Ascending four-limb weakness with global areflexia, facial diplegia and bulbar weakness over 6 days after an upper respiratory infection, with CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 108 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS, meets Brighton level 1 [Brighton_2011].

FVC below 20 mL/kg and falling, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O and MEP below 40 cmH2O with bulbar weakness and a weak cough call for elective intubation; the decision rests on the trend, bulbar function, cough and fatigue, not one threshold [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Autonomic monitoring is mandatory throughout the acute phase.
The antecedent infection is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

specialized_test.impression: Severe acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely reduced conduction velocities, absent sural SNAPs bilaterally, absent F-waves and H-reflexes. Needle EMG: reduced recruitment without active denervation. Findings meet electrodiagnostic criteria for acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions, no red herrings; classic post-URI AIDP with bulbar weakness where the respiratory trend decides elective intubation.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Six-day ascending weakness with bilateral facial diplegia and areflexia, preceded by upper respiratory infection.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. C. is a 44-year-old teacher presenting with 6-day progressive ascending neurological symptoms. Three weeks prior she had a URI lasting 5 days. Beginning 6 days ago, she noted bilateral foot tingling then progressive leg weakness. She is now unable to walk. She developed bilateral facial drooping 2 days ago and mild slurred speech. She coughed on water this morning. She cannot rise from her classroom chair and was helped to the ED by her husband. She feels short of breath when lying flat. No prior neurological history.

neurological_exam.additional: Speaks in short sentences; weak cough; mild accessory muscle use. No paradoxical breathing.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral facial weakness — both forehead and lower face, symmetric. Mild dysarthria. Mild dysphagia on liquid swallow test. Gag diminished.
neurological_exam.gait: Cannot walk unassisted. Unable to rise from chair.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Upper extremity: shoulder abduction 4/5, grip 4+/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Global areflexia — absent bilaterally all tendon reflexes.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal paresthesias, stocking-glove distribution to mid-calf and wrists.
